leaders.notes: Became Belhaven's 10th president in January 1996 at age 34; had previously been one of the youngest college presidents in the US as president of Sterling College (Kansas) from 1989. Still serving as of 2026, making him one of the longest-tenured sitting university presidents in the country. His immediate predecessor, Newton Wilson (1986-95), and brief acting president Daniel C. Fredericks (1995) fall before the 1996 research window.

Bellarmine's third president; led the school's transformation from Bellarmine College to Bellarmine University (2000) and grew enrollment from 2,500 to nearly 4,000. Died unexpectedly in office on March 1, 2016 after 26 years as president. Start year (1990) precedes the 1996 research-window cutoff but is included because his tenure spans into it.

Longtime Bellarmine EVP (joined 1994) appointed interim president by the Board of Trustees immediately after McGowan's sudden death in March 2016; served until Susan Donovan's arrival and retired from the university in May 2017.

Bellarmine's fourth president and first woman to lead the university; began July 1, 2017 after a 32-year career at Loyola University Maryland. In spring 2026 she announced she will retire at the conclusion of her contract in summer 2027, so a presidential search is expected to open in the 2026-27 academic year.

Promoted internally from EVP to president in 1982 at age 32; grew enrollment roughly 75% and raised the average ACT score during his tenure. Resigned in 1999 to become president of Rhodes College in Memphis, where he served until 2017. Start year (1982) precedes the 1996 window cutoff but is included because his tenure spans into it.

Hired in April 2000, roughly eight months after Troutt's 1999 departure; no interim president was identified in available sources for that gap. Oversaw major campus expansion and enrollment growth from under 3,000 to over 8,000 students. Retired May 2021 after a sabbatical year, later serving as interim chancellor of Henderson State University starting August 2023.

Began as Belmont's president June 1, 2021, after serving as Baylor's EVP/Provost and, before that, as Dean of Duke Divinity School. The Belmont board extended his contract through May 2036, signaling long-term confidence in his leadership.

Bethel's fourth president, leading the school for 26 years and growing it from a regional Bible college into a national Christian university; hired Jay Barnes as provost in 1995. Named president emeritus after retiring in 2008 and passed away in December 2021. Start year (1982) precedes the 1996 window cutoff but is included because his tenure spans into it.

Bethel's fifth president; had joined as provost in 1995 after 15 years leading student development at Messiah College. Retired June 30, 2020, and subsequently became president of the Christian College Consortium.

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Financial Officer and VP for Business and Finance
leaders.notes: First Bethel alumnus ('84) to lead the university, becoming its sixth president on July 1, 2020. Previously spent 25 years at Medtronic in corporate transformation roles before moving into higher-ed administration at Azusa Pacific. Still serving as of 2026.
